narrative:
The model estimates a 59% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your current situation.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest reason pushing the model toward predicting you might leave. Most employees the model expects to stay have longer track records, so your limited experience signals higher turnover risk to the system.

The second most important factor was that you have not received other job offers while working here. Surprisingly, this actually pulled the prediction slightly toward you staying, as having external opportunities often strongly predicts departure.

Third, your sense that it is difficult to get involved in decision-making and have your opinions heard at work was the factor that most strongly pushed the prediction toward leaving. This experience of low engagement stands out compared with the majority of employees the model expects to stay, who report easier involvement.

Taken together, your shorter experience and challenges feeling involved at work outweighed the stabilizing effect of not having other offers, leading to the decision to deny the promotion.

Your organization should focus on improving opportunities for meaningful involvement and faster career progression for early-career talent like yourself. You may want to discuss these specific concerns with your manager to see whether conditions can be improved before considering other opportunities. (218 words)
